official_measurement_examples.name: Level-crossing consultation trigger
official_measurement_examples.fact: ORR states that in England planning authorities must contact DfT and the relevant network operator where development could materially increase the volume or materially change the character of traffic using a level crossing.

official_measurement_examples.name: ORR permission limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: ORR explicitly states it does not approve or grant permission for new or reinstated level crossings; any legal right to cross must be established separately.

official_measurement_examples.name: Asset-protection role
official_measurement_examples.fact: Network Rail ASPRO supports works on or near railway infrastructure with safety assurance, engineering and access interfaces; engagement is not itself planning permission or land access authority.

official_measurement_examples.name: Third-party agreements
official_measurement_examples.fact: Network Rail publishes template asset-protection and development agreements for third-party works, showing contractual arrangements are distinct from statutory planning consent.

official_measurement_examples.name: Precautionary-area limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Network Rail identifies works in designated precautionary areas of level crossings as a type of work requiring asset-protection attention; this must not be converted into a universal development exclusion distance.

official_measurement_examples.name: Crossing order distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: ORR makes level crossing orders under the Level Crossings Act framework for specified protection arrangements; an order is not a parcel development permission.

official_measurement_examples.name: Risk assessment requirement
official_measurement_examples.fact: ORR guidance expects level-crossing risks to be actively managed and alternatives considered where reasonably practicable; generic proximity does not substitute for proposal-specific risk assessment.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning and railway rights separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning permission, railway asset-protection agreement, crossing rights, highway rights and railway safety approvals are separate controls and must not be inferred from one another.

core_rules: railway proximity is not a legal access right
ASPRO engagement is not planning permission
a level crossing order is not development consent
ORR does not grant legal rights for new or reinstated crossings
material traffic change at a level crossing is a consultation trigger not automatic refusal
railway asset-protection agreements are distinct from planning permission
a precautionary area must not be converted into a universal statutory setback
railway geometry does not prove ownership boundaries
railway operational data is not parcel development capacity
risk assessment must remain proposal and crossing specific
historic crossing status must retain date and legal instrument
Network Rail standards do not replace local planning requirements
planning permission does not automatically grant railway access
railway consultation does not reserve development capacity
no parcel railway clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
